CF-LSC0-6.schemaShare: The schema enforces it: encrypted_private_key CHECK accepts only the vault IdentityService ciphertext envelope (json_valid with text ciphertext, iv and salt); operation fingerprint CHECK accepts only a 64-char lowercase sha256 hex digest; no column is named for a password or secret. A plaintext key, a password-shaped fingerprint or a password column is a CHECK/RED failure (migration test CF-LSC0-6 row).

carryIn.otherLsc0CarryForwards: CF-LSC0-8/15/16/17 (counter and window semantics) are LSC-1S/LSC-1; LSC-1DB only stores durable failed_attempts and locked_until_ms.
carryIn.CF-LSC0-8: Persistence share: failed_attempts and locked_until_ms are durable columns (NOT NULL, default 0, CHECK >= 0) that survive close/reopen and a migration re-apply (proved in the migration suite). How revoke keeps and re-provision clears them is repository behaviour, routed to LSC-1S (its repository writes revoked_at without touching the counter and resets both on re-provision).
carryIn.CF-LSC0-16: Persistence share: only the per-seat failure count and lock deadline are persisted. The route-wide attempt windows (mint and operator) are process-local service state and are not stored, so a restart reopens the window but never the per-seat lock. Post-lock-expiry counter semantics and whether lock/concurrency refusals consume the window are routed to LSC-1S/LSC-1.
